January 1, 1971
2014-12-13T18:29:54+06:00 | The Daily Star
https://www.thedailystar.net/january-1-1971-53744

Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, chairman of Pakistan People’s Party, says in Karachi that he has postponed his proposed Dhaka tour. He is expected to meet Awami League chief Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in Dhaka on January 3. He tells reporters that the visit is cancelled for unavoidable circumstances since he had to visit six electoral constituencies of West Pakistan National Council on January 17. He offers to send Punjab People’s Party’s General Secretary Golam Mostafa Khar to meet Sheikh Mujib. Bhutto could not reach Sheikh Mujib on the phone, and says he had to cancel Khar’s plane ticket.

Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman meets five leaders of Kashmir Muslim Council, led by Khaja Sanaullah Shamim, and assures full support to alleviate the problems of Kashmir. On behalf of Sardar Abdhul Qayyum, president of Azad Kashmir, the Kashmiri leaders convey a letter of congratulation for Awami League in the historical election of 1970.

Awami League General Secretary Tajuddin Ahmed tells a gathering that the victory of Al-Fateha, Palestine fighters, is sure for its unrelenting fight to retrieve their motherland. Because the victory of truth and right is certain. He speaks at the sixth anniversary of Palestine Revolution organised at Engineers Institute.
